title: Trump’s Canada Tariffs Rely on Untested Law
partialText: The president has invoked a long dormant section of law to hit one of America’s closest allies, a move that has troubled courts in the past.

title: China Pushes Back After Trump Tightens the Screws on Iran
partialText: The Trump administration risks a clash with Beijing as it tries to cut off Iran’s economic lifelines without upending a fragile U.S.-China truce.

title: The Heat on Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent Grows
partialText: Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent’s plans to intervene in bond markets have drawn widespread criticism, including from a prominent former mentor.

title: This A.I. Start-Up Aims to Reverse the Backlash Against Data Centers
partialText: Emerald AI, now valued at $1.05 billion, uses software to keep power demand at the computing facilities from getting out of control.

title: Target Apologizes and Drops Halloween Costume Criticized as Racist
partialText: The children’s costume evoked blackface imagery, critics said. “We know we got this wrong, and we are deeply sorry,” the retailer said in response.

title: Is It Time for This 95-Year-Old Pianist to Retire?
partialText: Her vision and hearing are deteriorating, but she still wants to feel like she’s on top.

title: Many N.F.L. Players Get Brain Disease. Why Hasn’t OSHA Intervened?
partialText: “We never see things that are this dire,” a former chief scientist of the agency said about rates of C.T.E. in former players.

title: U.S. Tariffs Could Price Canadian Firms Out of U.S. and Threaten Thousands of Jobs
partialText: The 50 percent tariffs President Trump imposed on Canadian exports to the United States will make it impossible for many Canadian companies to continue to sell to the U.S. market, economists say.

title: S.E.C. Investigating Near-Implosion of A.I. Hedge Fund
partialText: Regulators sent subpoenas to major Wall Street banks seeking information about the trading of Situational Awareness, three people briefed on the outreach said.

title: What’s Behind the U.S. Treasury’s Latest Attempt to Lower Interest Rates
partialText: The Treasury Department said it could begin to buy back more of its debt, and bond market investors are assessing the potential effects on borrowing costs.

title: How Farmers Are Staying Afloat as Crop Prices Plunge
partialText: Most U.S. farmers will lose money this year. Landowners and investors are increasingly trying to make money from their land, not what can be grown from it.

title: Trump Threatens New 50% Tariffs on Cars, Trucks and Steel as U.S.-Canada Trade War Unfolds
partialText: President Trump vowed to increase tariffs on cars, trucks, auto parts and steel to 50 percent starting Jan. 1, as the countries edged toward a full-blown trade war.

title: Canada Is Retaliating Against Trump’s Tariffs. Will Others Follow?
partialText: Prime Minister Mark Carney’s decision to retaliate against U.S. tariffs has drawn praise from China, and exposed a rift in the Trump administration.

title: Research Firm’s Founder Explains $6 Million Payment to Fired Forbes Editor
partialText: RJ Shook of Shook Research said he paid Randall Lane, the former top editor at Forbes, for “services and guidance” in partnering with Forbes and later selling his research firm.

title: Washington Post Ordered to Rehire Fired Columnist Karen Attiah
partialText: An arbitrator ordered the newspaper to reinstate Karen Attiah, who was fired after posting about “white men who espouse hatred and violence” following Charlie Kirk’s killing.

title: Oil Prices Fall Ahead of U.S. Vow to Intensify Economic War Against Iran
partialText: Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent is expected to announce an escalation of sanctions aimed at further isolating Iranian trade.

title: Los Angeles Dodgers Owner’s Troubles Roil Insurance World
partialText: Federal investigations of Mark Walter’s business empire have put a spotlight on private-equity-owned insurers that invest premiums in risky assets.

title: Netflix, YouTube and Amazon Want You to Watch Everything From One App: Theirs
partialText: YouTube is racing to catch up to Amazon, which already offers users the chance to subscribe to services like HBO Max from within its app. Netflix is increasingly open to the idea, too.

title: Maker of Clear Eyes Recalls Nearly 40,000 Bottles Over Contamination Risk
partialText: Federal safety regulators said the maker of Clear Eyes Maximum Itchy Eye Relief voluntarily recalled the drops because of a “lack of assurance of sterility.”

title: Dr. Dre and Jimmy Iovine Think A.I. Is Good for Music
partialText: The hit-making duo turned tech moguls also have thoughts about why corporate America isn’t collaborative enough.

title: How Big Tech Captured American Schools
partialText: Companies like Google and Microsoft have used their money, their might and their massive reach to influence nearly every step of the education supply chain.

title: The U.S. Start-Up Making Low-Cost Interceptors for the Iran War
partialText: For Florida-based Powerus, becoming a global supplier of counterdrone technology has meant involving the Trumps, a golf course and a new way of doing business.

title: Four Years Ago, a Crypto Boss Went Missing. Now His Successor Has.
partialText: The mysterious collapse of a European cryptocurrency exchange helps to explain why the industry hasn’t shaken off its reputation as a magnet for criminals.

title: Trump’s Top Trade Representative Details Offer That Canada Rejected
partialText: In an interview, Jamieson Greer, President Trump’s trade representative, laid out details of what the United States offered to Canada before talks crumbled.

title: U.S. Economy Could Feel the Sting From Trade War With Canada
partialText: A tit-for-tat trade fight between the two allies could create new headaches for consumers and businesses already stung by high prices.

title: Paramount and California to Hold Preliminary Talks on Warner Bros. Deal
partialText: The discussions on Monday are an early effort to resolve a lawsuit that California and 11 other states filed to block Paramount’s $111 billion acquisition of Warner Bros. Discovery.

title: Harvard Is Selling a $699 Course Taught by A.I. Clones of Its Faculty
partialText: To create a new bootcamp for entrepreneurs, Harvard Business School made A.I. avatars of its instructors.

title: The Economy Got Used to Low Borrowing Costs. Their Exit Could Pose Risks.
partialText: After roughly two decades of ultralow interest rates, a period of rapid readjustment is ahead for the United States, the world’s largest economy and most important financial system.

title: What if Your Texts Traveled as Slowly as a Carrier Pigeon?
partialText: Apps that let users send digital messages at ultraslow speeds have taken off, with users reveling in a slower pace of life. (Just don’t use the them to make dinner plans.)

title: Gen Z Is Building Wealth By Investing Instead of Buying Homes
partialText: When it comes to building wealth, Gen Z is more focused on investment apps and their retirement accounts than they are in building equity in a home.

title: Universal’s New Coaster Is a Scream. That’s the Problem.
partialText: The Hollywood theme park built a “whisper quiet” ride to avoid angering nearby neighbors. They didn’t fully account for the enthusiasm of the riders.

title: Boeing Engineers and Technicians Reject Contract Offer
partialText: The union members also authorized a potential strike if a new agreement is not reached by October.

title: Overlooked No More: Patricia Douglas, Who Challenged Hollywood’s Culture of Abuse
partialText: Eight decades before the #MeToo groundswell, she took MGM to court after alleging she was attacked at a studio party in 1937.

title: Meghan of Sussex Eyes Role in Netflix Show ‘The Gentlemen’
partialText: The duchess’s representatives have had exploratory talks about her joining a third season of “The Gentlemen,” two people said. Netflix has not yet ordered a third season of the show.

title: Mark Zuckerberg Buys an Irish Castle
partialText: The prominent landowner has added a nearly 200-year-old estate to his holdings. Archival information says it can take “a brisk walk of 4½ minutes to reach the dining room from the kitchen.”

title: Trump Announces Move to Lift Ground Beef Tariffs in Bid to Lower Prices
partialText: The move prompted blowback from cattle ranchers and Republicans who represent them.

title: In China’s Biggest Car Recall, Tesla and 8 Others Will Address Door Safety
partialText: China’s regulator ordered changes after vehicle occupants sometimes had difficulty exiting electric cars, an issue that has led to lawsuits against Tesla in the United States.

title: Shein, a Fast-Fashion Giant, Struggles to Grow Ahead of a Much-Delayed IPO
partialText: Facing pressure in the United States and Europe, Shein is struggling to find new ways to grow ahead of its much-delayed initial public offering.

title: Victor Niederhoffer, Trader Who Went Boom and Bust (Twice), Dies at 82
partialText: He pioneered a technique for using computers to predict short-term movements in stock prices, something that proved to be hugely lucrative — when it worked.

title: Do You Need Flood Insurance? What to Know Ahead of Peak Hurricane Season.
partialText: No hurricane-strength storms have formed yet this year in the Atlantic basin, but the limiting activity isn’t certain to continue.

title: Can Bessent’s ‘Big Tool Kit’ Calm Bond Investors?
partialText: Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent has vowed to step up efforts to restore calm to the debt markets. So far, it’s not working out that way.

title: Stocks and Bonds Steady at the End of a Tumultuous Week
partialText: Fears about the war in Iran, government deficits, the economy and corporate borrowing stirred global markets.

title: Should You Invest in Bonds Right Now?
partialText: High-quality bonds are still safer than stocks, but they have been swinging in value, so move cautiously, our columnist says.

title: Why Cruise Line Are Hiking Certain Fees
partialText: Some major lines are increasing gratuities and deposit requirements, and charging more for certain packages. It’s all adding up.

title: Iran War Raises Risk of Collisions and Oil Spills in Strait of Hormuz
partialText: More vessels are navigating the Strait of Hormuz with their location devices turned off to evade attacks by Iran, adding to the threat of collisions.

title: Why Porsche, Bentley and Other Car Brands Entered Miami’s Condo Market
partialText: Pagani, Bentley, Aston Martin and other high-end automakers are teaming up with residential developers, solidifying the city as having the most branded residences associated with car brands in the nation.

title: Seattle Times Columnist Resigns After Paper Scrapped Trans Sports Column
partialText: Matt Calkins, a longtime sports columnist, said editors had refused to publish a column about transgender athletes in women’s competitions.

title: The New York Times Loses Defamation Lawsuit in Alabama
partialText: A 2023 article incorrectly reported that a University of Alabama basketball player was at the scene of a deadly shooting. A jury awarded $9.25 million in damages.

title: How Big Tech’s A.I. Borrowing Binge Is Driving Up Bond Yields
partialText: Analysts said the recent rise in Treasury yields partly reflected investor expectations that A.I.-driven growth could keep interest rates elevated.

title: Two Binance Employees Detained in the U.A.E. Amid Police Inquiries
partialText: The detentions of the workers, who have been released, are a sign of legal pressure that the world’s largest crypto exchange faces in the Emirates, which is home to its main regulator.
